title: Customer edge change sentinel and forensics protocol (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose:
This PRD drafts a lightweight on-customer-network change detection and forensics protocol ("edge sentinel") to complement Private deployments. The goal is to provide: a minimal, auditable trace of customer-managed networking changes relevant to inference runtime reachability and security; robust approval gate hooks with signed attestations; and a practical post-incident forensics pack that customers and Redwood on-call can jointly use without exposing customer secrets.

Context / problem statement:
- Customers running Redwood Private manage their own VPCs, firewalls, and on-prem connectivity. Network changes (route updates, firewall policy edits, peering changes) can silently break routing to inference nodes or cause data-plane exposure.
- Current telemetry is focused on control-plane events and host-level metrics. We lack a structured, searchable timeline of customer-side network changes and the approvals/attestations that allowed them.
- When incidents occur we spend hours collecting disparate logs (customer console screenshots, support chat threads, SRE notes). We need a standard artifact set and a gating mechanism to reduce repeat incident triage time.

Goals:
- Define a minimal event schema for customer-network-change events (who, what, why, when, affected CIDRs, rollback hints).
- Attach a cryptographic attestation token to approval gates (signed approval id + operator identity + TTL) that Redwood can verify without storing customer credentials.
- Provide a forensics pack generator (on-customer and control-plane stubs) that can be assembled quickly and shared under an agreed process.
- Implement sentinel sampling and anomaly scoring so high-risk changes trigger stronger approvals / advisory modes.

Non-goals:
- We will not ship full packet-capture or mandatory remote debugging access.
- This is not an automated network remediation system (no auto-rollbacks by Redwood).

Feature scope (high level):
1) Event schema and transport
   - Schema fields: event_id, timestamp, operator_id, operator_email, approval_id, action_type (route-add, route-remove, firewall-mod, peering, NAT-change, BGP-ann), affected_resources (list of CIDRs / peering ids), intended-window (start/end), change_tokens (pre/post config hashes), human_reason (free text), confidence_level (manual, automated), evidence_refs (urls or artifact ids).
   - Transport: customers push events to a short-lived signed webhook endpoint we provide, or we accept pre-signed manifests attached to approval artifacts. Webhook supports gzip, JSONL for batching.

2) Approval gates & attestations
   - Gate levels: advisory (email/console notice), standard (single operator approval), high-risk (multi-operator or manager approval + 15-minute delayed window), emergency (override with audit escalation).
   - Attestation token: compact JWT-like token signed by customer KMS (or a Redwood-issued ephemeral key for customers who opt-in). Token contains approval_id, signer, level, timestamp, TTL, and a binding to event_id. Redwood validates signature + TTL + schema.
   - UI hooks: Console will display pending changes with link to attached attestation; operators can opt to require attestation before a configuration change is considered supported.

3) Forensics pack (shared artifact collection)
   - Minimal pack contents: event manifest (schema above), pre/post config diffs (route tables, firewall rules), topology snapshot (annotated list of subnets, peers, gateways), short pcap/flow logs if customer elects (optional, must be provided as customer-controlled encrypted blob), operator chat log excerpt (copy-paste), and Redwood control-plane correlation (timestamped API calls, host heartbeats, recent health checks).
   - Packaging: signed tarball with index.json and a README explaining the artifact provenance and how to decrypt (if encrypted).
   - Access model: customer can generate the pack and share an expiring link; Redwood support may request the pack via an authorization flow verified by the attestation token.

4) Sentinel detectors and scoring
   - Lightweight detectors that run on submitted manifests and runtime telemetry: sudden prefix additions, route overlaps with reserved ranges, simultaneous firewall-open + route-add, peering changes during heavy traffic.
   - Score: 0-100 with thresholds for advisory/standard/high-risk. Score factors: asset criticality (is this route to inference subnet?), change window (scheduled vs unscheduled), operator history, size/scope of CIDRs.

Operator experience and flows:
- Operator plans change in their tooling -> creates approval in their workflow -> issues attestation token bound to event_id -> submits event via webhook or uploads manifest to Redwood console.
- Redwood console shows pending change, detector score. For high scores, Redwood optionally blocks support requests until a multi-operator approval is present.
- Post-change, operator can trigger forensics-pack generation (or Redwood support can request it).

Security, privacy, and compliance notes:
- No customer secrets: attestation tokens should be verifiable without Redwood holding customer private keys unless customer opts in (ephemeral trusted-proxy flow).
- Data minimization: require only config diffs and metadata; flow logs/pcaps are optional and must be encrypted with customer-managed key.
- Retention: by default Redwood stores event-manifests and attestations for 90 days; for customers with longer retention needs we provide configurable export hooks (S3/GS).
- Auditability: all Redwood-side verifications and support requests that access a forensics pack are themselves logged and available to the customer as an audit trail.

Implementation considerations and risks:
- Customer ecosystem fragmentation (multiple vendors, on-prem tooling) means we must provide several ingestion options (webhook, S3 drop, manual upload).
- Signature verification: customers may not have KMS practices; provide fallback flow with Redwood-ephemeral-key and stronger SLA/trust terms.
- False positives on detector -> friction. Need a feedback loop where customers and Redwood can mark events as benign to tune scoring.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default attestation signing model: customer KMS (recommended) vs Redwood ephemeral signing (opt-in).
- What constitutes a multi-operator approval? time-window + identity from IdP?
- Retention SLAs for long-lived customers and eDiscovery requests.
- How do we integrate with existing ticketing (Zendesk/Jira) in a supported and auditable way?

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Within 3 months of MVP: support webhook ingestion, validate attestations (customer KMS) for 3 pilot customers, generate forensics pack on demand.
- Reduce median triage time for customer-network-caused incidents from current baseline by 40% for pilot cohort.
- Detector precision > 80% at advisory threshold after two months of tuning with pilot data.

Milestones (tentative):
- Week 0-3: finalize schema, approval-level UX mocks, validate signature verification approach.
- Week 4-8: implement ingestion endpoints + attestation verification + console pending-change surface. Run 2 pilot tests.
- Week 9-12: forensics pack generator, packaging, and access flow. SDLC + security review.
- Week 13-16: detector scoring, feedback loop, pilot expansion to 6 customers.

Dependencies:
- IdP integration for operator identity assertions (eng: platform-auth).
- Support tools for pack exchange (eng: console-and-tooling + infra).
- Legal review for data sharing and eDiscovery (legal/compliance).

Notes / TODOs:
- Draft the minimal JSON schema in this doc (next iteration).
- Capture sample manifests from two pilot customers to tune detectors.
- Create a short runbook for on-call engineers describing how to request and validate a forensics pack.

Appendix: quick sample event (illustrative)
{
  event_id: "evt-20241114-0001",
  timestamp: "2024-11-14T15:02:12Z",
  operator_id: "idp:okta|U0234",
  operator_email: "netops@custco.com",
  approval_id: "app-98712",
  action_type: "route-add",
  affected_resources: ["10.8.21.0/24"],
  change_tokens: { pre: "sha256:abc...", post: "sha256:def..." },
  human_reason: "add route for new inference cluster",
  confidence_level: "manual",
  evidence_refs: ["s3://custco-forensics/evt-98712/pre-config.json"]
}

Feedback welcome — this is an early draft aimed at getting alignment from product, eng, and legal. If you are listed as a collaborator please add inline comments or add sample manifests from customer pilots to the linked Confluence page.
